# Game model (7 levels)

## Rendering
- Background grid cell = 8 px. Game "unit" = 24 px (3x3 cells). Objects snap to 24px units.
- Unit coords: ucol = floor(x/24)... (actually pieces are 24px blocks aligned to 8px grid; use pixel bounds).
- Light gray (#CCCCCC) = floor/passable. Medium gray (#999999) = void/wall.
- Purple (#A356D6) = special region (blocked white beam in L1; a launched piece slid through it).
- Green blocks (#4FCC30) with an inner dark shape = movable pieces.
  - Inner shape WHITE = currently selected piece. Inner shape BLACK = unselected.
- Black-outlined (#333) rectangles = goals. Outline drawn 1 cell (8px) outside the goal
  area, so goal interior = the piece-sized area. Pieces have matching shapes/sizes.

## Controls
- ACTION6 (click on a piece) = select that piece.
- ACTION1/2/3/4 = move selected piece Up/Down/Left/Right by exactly 1 unit (24px).
  Blocked by walls (no visual change, action wasted).
- ACTION5 not available. ACTION7 (undo) not offered in L1.
- Level completes when every piece rests on its matching goal.

## Observed interaction (L1)
- Moving the selected piece INTO an adjacent unselected piece did not move the selected
  piece; instead the other piece was launched and slid several units in that direction
  (5 units, passing straight through the purple wall) before stopping.
- A white beam is drawn from the selected piece rightward until it hits purple (meaning unclear).

## L1 solution shape

# Game model (7 levels)

## Rendering / geometry
- Background grid cell = 8 px (64x64 cells). Movement unit = 3 cells = 24 px.
- Pieces are green (#4FCC30) rectangles, size k x m units, with a dark inner rectangle.
  Inner WHITE = selected piece; inner BLACK = unselected.
- Goals are dark (#333) rectangular OUTLINES ("goal boxes"): outline is 1 cell thick and
  sits 1 cell OUTSIDE the goal interior. Interior = exactly one piece footprint.
  Each piece has one goal of the same shape/size.
- Floor #CCCCCC = walkable. #999999 = solid wall. Purple #A356D6 = NOT walkable, but
  sliding (launched) pieces pass straight through it.

## Controls
- ACTION6 (click on a piece) = select that piece.
- ACTION1/2/3/4 = Up/Down/Left/Right, move selected piece exactly 1 unit.
  Blocked by walls/purple => nothing happens (action wasted).
- ACTION5 unavailable; ACTION7 (undo) not offered.
- Level complete when all pieces sit on their matching goal interiors.

## LAUNCH mechanic (key)
- If the selected piece presses a direction toward an ADJACENT piece, the selected piece
  does NOT move; the other piece is LAUNCHED and slides in that direction, 1 unit/frame.
- A launched piece slides through purple and floor and stops when:
  * it would hit a wall, or
  * it first OVERLAPS any goal box outline (its own or another's), or
  * it hits another piece -> that piece is pushed too (chain); they end up flush.
- Pieces already touching a goal box before launch: untested (avoid).
- Because a piece stops on first contact with a goal box's outline, it never lands
  directly in a goal; you must select it and walk it in.

## Strategy
Use launches only to cross purple barriers between rooms; walk pieces normally otherwise.
Order moves so the "pusher" is orthogonally adjacent with overlapping rows/cols.

# Game model (7 levels)

## Rendering / geometry
- Background grid cell = 8 px (64x64 cells). Movement unit = 3 cells = 24 px.
- Pieces are colored polyominoes made of unit blocks (1x1, 2x1, 2x2, plus-pentomino...).
  GREEN (#4FCC30) pieces are player-selectable. YELLOW (#FFDC00) pieces appear in L3
  (probably push-only). A green piece's inner mark: WHITE = selected, BLACK = not.
- Goals are dark (#333) 1-cell-thick OUTLINES drawn 1 cell OUTSIDE a piece-shaped area.
  Goal interior == exactly one piece footprint of matching shape.
- #CCCCCC floor walkable; #999999 solid wall; purple #A356D6 blocks WALKING but
  launched (sliding) pieces pass through it.

## Controls
- ACTION6 click on a piece = select it.
- ACTION1/2/3/4 = Up/Down/Left/Right: move selected piece 1 unit. Blocked => no change.
- Level completes when every piece rests exactly on its matching goal interior.

## LAUNCH rule (verified L1, L2, predicted L3)
- If the selected piece presses a direction toward an ADJACENT piece, the selected piece
  does NOT move; the other piece is LAUNCHED and slides that direction.
- Slide distance = exactly 5 UNITS (120 px), moving 1 unit per animation frame.
- Exception: if the 5-unit stop would leave the piece overlapping purple, it keeps
  sliding until completely clear of purple.
- If it runs into another piece, that piece is pushed along (chain); they end flush and
  the whole chain obeys the same stop rule.
- Goal outlines do NOT block anything (walking or sliding). A launched piece can land
  directly in its goal if the distance is exactly 5 units.
- Walls stop a slide (untested but assumed).

## Strategy
Levels are designed so required travel distances are multiples of 5 units for launched
pieces. Compute unit coordinates for pieces/goals first, then route the controllable
piece to the pushing squares.

# Block-puzzle game — COMPLETED (7/7 levels, WIN at turn 302)

## Rendering / geometry
- Background cell = 8 px (64x64 grid). Movement unit = 3 cells = 24 px.
  Each level has its own unit-grid offset; derive it from piece/goal pixel bounds
  (all pieces and goal interiors are unit-aligned; walls are NOT necessarily).
- A unit square is usable only if all 9 of its cells are floor.
- Colors: #CCCCCC floor, #999999 wall, #A356D6 purple (blocks WALKING, but launched or
  piston-shoved pieces pass through it), #4FCC30 green pieces (selectable),
  #FFDC00 yellow pieces (push-only), #921231 dark-red pistons, #FF851B orange charge bar.
- Goals = #333 1-cell-thick outlines drawn 1 cell OUTSIDE a piece-shaped area. Outlines are
  pure decoration: they never block walking or sliding.
- Piece shapes vary (1x1, 2x1, 1x2, 2x2, plus-pentomino). Each piece matches one same-shape goal.

## Controls
- ACTION6 = click a piece to select it. IMPORTANT: a click does NOT advance the piston clock.
- ACTION1/2/3/4 = move the selected piece 1 unit up/down/left/right. Blocked => nothing moves,
  but the piston clock still ticks (useful as a timed no-op).
- Level completes the instant every piece rests on its matching goal interior.

## LAUNCH rule
- Selected piece presses toward an ADJACENT piece => the OTHER piece is LAUNCHED; the pusher
  never moves. Partial face contact is enough.
- Slide distance = exactly 5 UNITS, 1 unit per animation frame.
- If the 5-unit resting spot would overlap purple, it keeps sliding until fully clear.
- Walls / other pieces stop it early (it rests at the last legal unit); a hit piece is pushed
  along in a chain and the whole chain obeys the same rules.
- Pressing into a piece that cannot move at all is a free no-op (great for piston timing).

## PISTON rule (dark-red blocks)
- Orange charge bar grows 1 cell per MOVEMENT action, filling from the piston's BACK edge.
  Capacity = piston length along its axis in cells (2x2 => 6 actions, 1x1 => 3).
- When full it FIRES: extends 3 units out of its FRONT face (the side opposite the bar),
  shoving any piece in front by 3 units (extended further if it would land on purple),
  then retracts and resets. Then it recharges.
- Pistons are ordinary pieces for launching purposes: relocating a piston with launches is
  often the only way to reach a sealed region.

## Solving method that worked
1. Read the board with read_pixels line-scans; build a unit map of floor/wall/purple.
2. Identify connected regions and which barriers require launches or piston shoves.
3. Assign each piece to its same-shape goal; check that every piece can still reach its goal
   after each crossing (a piece launched into a sealed region can never come back).
4. Plan pusher positions, then schedule around the piston clock (fires every 6 movement actions),
   using blocked-direction presses as no-ops to align timing.

## Summary of the model I built

**Core mechanics discovered:**
- Board is a 64×64 cell grid; pieces move in 3-cell "units". Green pieces are selectable (click = ACTION6), yellow/red ones are only pushable.
- **Launch rule:** pressing toward an adjacent piece launches *that* piece exactly **5 units** (the pusher stays put), extended further if it would come to rest on purple, stopped early by walls/pieces (with chain-pushing).
- **Purple** blocks walking but is transparent to launched/shoved pieces — it's the barrier that forces the launch puzzles.
- **Goal outlines are decoration** — they never block anything (this took a couple of contradictory observations to pin down).
- **Dark-red pistons** (L5–L7): an orange bar fills 1 cell per movement action from the back edge; when full the piston extends 3 units out of its front face, shoving whatever is there, then retracts. Clicks don't advance that clock — which mattered for timing.

**Key insights per level:** L1–L2 established launch distance; L3 confirmed exactly-5-unit slides; L4 combined launches with purple crossings; L5 revealed pistons and required a timed approach; L6 needed relocating a piston to ride it across a purple band twice; L7's top-left room was a sealed trap, so the solution was to **launch the piston itself two rooms to the left** so it could shove the yellow plus out — no green piece ever had to enter the one-way region.
